newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Rebels say Sri Lankan forces pound northern town.
newsitem.headline: Rebels say Sri Lankan forces pound northern town.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops, poised to take complete control of a northern Tamil rebel-held town, pounded the area with artillery and air strikes, the rebels said on Friday.
The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) said in a statement that army artillery and air force planes hammered the town of Puliyankulam in the heartland of the mostly shrub-covered Wanni region.

The statement, issued by the LTTE's London office, said Puliyankulam town and surrounding areas were being bombarded by the military after the rebels staged a daring attack on one of its flanks last Tuesday.
Military officials in the north told Reuters troops on Friday were consolidating in the areas that came under attack.
Military spokesman Brigadier Sarath Munasinghe told a news conference on Thursday that troops were in the general area of Puliyankulam.
The army's advance into the rebel stronghold has been slowed by two rebel attacks in as many weeks on the advancing troops' tail, which has left scores of soldiers and rebels dead.
The military launched Operation "Jaya Sikuru", or "Sure of Victory" last month in a bid to open a highway from Vavuniya to the Jaffna peninsula, a further 100 km (60 miles) north.
Vavuniya lies 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo.
On Tuesday, more than 1,000 LTTE rebels attacked the army's artillery and mortar positions near Periyamadu, just south of Puliyankulam.
The Defence Ministry said four officers and 60 soldiers were killed and 68 were wounded in the attack. It said 150 rebels also died and a large number were wounded.
The LTTE said more than 100 soldiers and 85 rebels were killed, but military officials in the north have put the toll from both sides at more than 300.
Munasinghe said the attack would not affect the military's thrust into the rebels' stronghold. He said it showed the rebels were desperately trying to stop the army's advance further north.
The LTTE are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the ethnic war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
